links.reason: Kural 1269 counts days toward a fixed return (வருநாள்வைத்து ஏங்குபவர்க்கு); Ainkurunuru 350 says the fixed time itself has come (தான்வந் தன்றே ... தெளிக்கும் பொழுதே) and he has not (அவரோ வாரார). The pair shows waiting with a date against the date passing empty, which neither verse shows alone.

Both have the stag with its mate (இரலைதன் இன்புறு துணையொடு, Kuruntokai 65; இரலை ... மடப்பிணை அருத்தி, Akananuru 34), seen by the waiting woman as a reproach (இருந்திரோ) and by the returning man as a spur (செல்க, தேரே). The reading from both ends is real, but it is a shared image, not one verse limiting the other.

Ainkurunuru 217 asks why the body pales even though he comes (வரவுமிவண் மேனி பசப்பது எவன்கொல்), and Kural 1187 makes pallor follow the least gap in embrace (புடைபெயர்ந்தேன் அவ்வளவில்). The poem names no cause, so 'visits ending in parting' is the linker's answer; the speaker is not fixed as the friend either (அன்னாய் can be the heroine's address).

The crab with its mate is shared (தன்துணையோடு ஆடும் அலவன், Thinaimalai 40; வீழ்துணைக்கு இடூஉம் அலவன், Akananuru 380). But in Thinaimalai 40 she watches the crab before he answers and goes (போயினான் சென்றான் comes last), not 'alone after he dismissed her ache and went', so the teaches misstates the poem's order, and the venba's text is obscure.

Kalittokai 47 has the man put off his manliness (தன் ஆண்தகை விட்டு) to say he will not live if she leaves (வாழலேன் யான் ... நீ நீப்பின்), and has the girl weigh shame (நாண் அடப் பெயர்த்தல் நமக்கும் ஒல்லாது). Kural 1133 is his own inventory of lost நாண் and ஆண்மை with the madal as threat, so the pair gives both sides of one pressure.

Both read mullai buds as teeth (கூர்எயிறு ஈன, Kainnilai 25; முள்ளெயி றேய்ப்ப, Kar Narpathu 21), one at home as the friend's assurance (வருவர்நம் காதலர்) and one on the road home. It is a shared image read at two ends, not a development of one idea.
links.text_issue: Kar Narpathu 21's colophon reads தலைமகள் பாகற்குச் சொல்லியது, likely an error for தலைமகன், since the speaker rides the chariot.

links.reason: Both rank love's burning above fire (தீயினும் கடிது அவர் சாயலின் கனலும் நோய்; தொடிற்சுடின் அல்லது ... விடிற்சுடல்). But the paradoxes differ: Kalittokai says his gentleness burns, the Kural says love burns from a distance, so the Kural does not compress the kali's three steps, and 'end point of an argued rhetoric' is a claim of descent the texts do not support.

The breached dam is shared (வையை உடைந்த மடை அடைத்தக்கண்ணும் பின்னும் மலிரும் பிசிர்; செறுத்தோறு உடைப்பினும் ... மறுத்தும் சிறைசெய்வர்). The Naladiyar never claims that re-damming stops the seepage, so the two are not incompatible; the Paripadal limits it (closing the breach does not end the hurt). 'Declares impossible' overstates the wife's words.
links.text_issue: Line 82 is uncertain in its first words.

links.reason: The near-verbatim motif of killing travellers who carry nothing (பொருளிலராயினும் ... எய்யும், Thinaimalai 84; கலனிலர் ஆயினும் கொன்று, Akananuru 375) is real, and the timing differs: செல்பவோ is before departure, இறந்தோர் after. The teaches is true but thin, since it only notes a stock road-danger used at two moments.

Kuruntokai 40 first denies every tie of kin (யாயும் ஞாயும் யாரா கியரோ ... எவ்வழி யறிதும்) and then has the hearts mingle (செம்புலப் பெயனீர் போல ... கலந்தனவே). Kural 1122's bond is body and life (உடம்பொடு உயிரிடை), a pair that is never apart. The contrast between union made from strangers and union given by nature is specific and true.

The fancy is nearly identical (நெஞ்சத்துஉள் ஓடி ஒளித்து, Kalittokai 144.57; விழிக்குங்கால் நெஞ்சத்தர் ஆவர் விரைந்து, Kural 1218), and the kali turns it to accusation (துஞ்சா நோய் செய்யும் அறன் இல் அவன்). Since the valuations differ, this is a shared image, not 'agrees'.

Ainkurunuru 53 asks why the ford should afflict (துறைஎவன் அணங்கும்) when the sickness is his oath (நீயுற்ற சூளே); Kuruntokai 53 places that oath at the town's ford, with her forearm held (எம்மூர் வியன்துறை நேரிறை முன்கை பற்றி), and brings in the velan's veri ground. Together they turn the possession diagnosis into a charge of perjury. Note: சூரரமகளிர் are not specifically water goddesses.

Ainkurunuru 70 sets the clean, fragrant women (தூயர் நறியர்நின் பெண்டிர்) against the wife who bore a son (பேஎய் அனையம்யாம் சேய்பயந் தனமே); Akananuru 26 shows him shrinking from the milk (தீம்பால் படுதல் தாம் அஞ்சினரே) and her saying 'you suit the good women'. The pair names the nursing body as the ground of the contrast, which neither states alone.

Kural 1265 makes sight the cure (கண்ணாரக் கண்டபின் நீங்கும் ... பசப்பு); Ainkurunuru 459 makes it embrace (பசலை தீரப் புல்லவும்) and doubts it (இயைவது கொல்லோ) because he went with the king (வேந்தனொடு சென்ற). The qualification is specific and in the Tamil.

The unaimed look and smile (குறியா நோக்கமொடு முறுவல் நல்கி) match Kural 1094's sidelong look and soft smile, and the poem's question (நினக்கோ அறியுநள் நெஞ்சே) is doubt. But the confinement that the teaches turns on comes from the colophon (இச்செறிப்பின் பிற்றை ஞான்று), not the poem, and 'depends on continued access' generalizes beyond both.

Both send a creature to the shore lord (அலவ ... நீயே சொல்லல் வேண்டும்; புணர்அன்றில் ... உரையாய்). But Akananuru 170 also sets a paired creature as reproach (கடற்சிறு காக்கை காமர் பெடையொடு ... கனவும்), so the 'reach first, example second' contrast does not hold. A creature as messenger is a stock device.

Both use the maxim about men and work (வினையே ஆடவர்க் குயிரே; செயல்படு மனத்தர் செய்பொருட்கு அகல்வர் ஆடவர்) to reach opposite conclusions (அழுங்குவர் செலவே as against நன்று செய்தனையே). These are different situations turning a common saying, not incompatible claims. The teaches itself says the argument lies in what each adds, which is qualification.

Ainkurunuru 451 hands endurance in the camp to the king (ஆற்றவும் இருத்தல் வேந்தனது தொழிலே); 460 concedes that the king does not tire of the camp (பெருஞ்சின வேந்தனும் பாசறை முனியான்) and that no message comes, ending in helplessness (என்ஆகு வன்கொல்). In the same decade the argument turns to recognition.
links.text_issue: Line 1 of 460 and line 1 of 451 are repaired readings.

links.reason: Both have the lover coming only into her heart (நெஞ்சத் தல்லது வரவறி யானே; எம்நெஞ்சத்து ஓவா வரல்). Kural 1205 calls it shameless (நாணார்கொல்), while Kuruntokai 302 offers a reason, fear of gossip (அலரதற் கஞ்சினன் கொல்லோ). Opposite verdicts on the same phantom visit are a true qualification.

Both address the moon, but with different requests: Kural 1210 asks it not to set (படாஅதி), and Natrinai 196 asks it to show where he hides (உள்வழி காட்டாய்) on pain of waning as a lying witness (அறி கரி பொய்த்தலின்). The Kural is not a compression of that argument, so the teaches claims a descent the texts do not show.

Both make his coming cure the pallor of her shoulders (பிணிநிறம் தீர்ந்து பெரும்பணைத்தோள் வீங்க; நீங்கும்என் மென்தோள் பசப்பு). The step 'the coming is the wedding itself' rests on reading the vengai (கணிநிறை வேங்கை) as a wedding sign, which the venba does not state.
links.text_issue: Line 2 has தோழ!, probably தோழி with a dropped vowel sign.

links.reason: Natrinai 194's parrot is one that no longer takes the millet ears the sickle has seized (இரும்பு கவர்கொண்ட ஏனல் பெருங் குரல் கொள்ளாச் சிறு பசுங் கிளி): the harvest is in and the watch is over, as the colophon (செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇயது) agrees. The note's 'did not take the ears while they played' and the teaches' 'keeps the field watch going' misread it. The thanks to parrots (யாம் எவன் செய்குவம் / கைம்மாறு யாது செய்வாம்) are a real echo, but the claimed opposition is false.

The same poet's two answers to the man's 'the waste is harsh' (இன்னா என்றிராயின்; கடுமைய காடு என்றால்): the friend makes the lonely house equally harsh (இனியவோ பெரும தமியோர்க்கு மனையே), and the woman makes shared hardship her joy (துன்பம் துணை ஆக ... இன்பமும் உண்டோ). The step from equal harm to the demand to go is specific.

Kuruntokai 30's dream is a lie that deceived her (பொய்க்கனா மருட்ட); Kalittokai 128's dream, told entirely in போலவும், holds her life at the brink in hope (நனவின் வருதலும் உண்டு ... நின்றது என் அரும் பெறல் உயிரே). These are different moments and outcomes, not incompatible claims about dreams, and Kalittokai also knows the dream is unreal.

Kalittokai 149 states that failing those who helped one in want strikes even one's descendants (ஒற்கத்துள் உதவியார்க்கு உதவாதான் ... எச்சத்துள் ஆயினும் ... எறியாது விடாதே) and applies it to the lover. This is Kural 110's no-escape rule for killing a benefit (உய்வில்லை செய்ந்நன்றி கொன்ற மகற்கு). Counting her as a benefactor is the friend's argument, and the pair makes it visible.

Thinaimalai 78's elephant finds no water (பருகுநீர் பைஞ்சுனையில் காணாது) as a measure of danger; Kalittokai 11's tusker gives the little water to its mate (பிடி ஊட்டிப் பின் உண்ணும் களிறு). The venba never presents its elephant as lone or mateless, so the 'paired against lone' contrast is the linker's construction on a stock drought image.

The boar was kept many days in a pit, fed rice flour and kept from its sow (பன்மயிர்ப் பிணவொடு பாயம் போகாது நென்மா வல்சி தீற்றிப் பன்னாள் குழிநிறுத்து ஓம்பிய), to be served with toddy. That is an animal raised to be eaten, exactly what Kural 256's argument from demand (தினற்பொருட்டால் கொல்லாது உலகெனின்) condemns, and the idyll offers it as reward. 'Sold' is implied by the toddy-sellers' houses, not stated.

புணர்வு is shared, and both find pain in union (புணர்வின் இன்னான்; புன்கண் உடைத்தால் புணர்வு). But the poem's own reason is rarity (அரும்புணர் வினனே, against the ever-embracing புணரி), not the fear of parting, so 'Valluvar gives the reason the poem leaves implicit' imposes the Kural's cause.

Purananuru 196 states the giver's fault as a rule (ஒல்லுவது இல்லென மறுத்தலும் ... புரப்போர் புகழ்குறை படூஉம்) and still blesses (நோயிலர் ஆகநின் புதல்வர்). Kural 1060 asks the asker not to be angry because the refuser may have cause. The poem shares the absence of anger but denies the Kural's ground, so it qualifies rather than agrees.

Both make evening a killer (கொலைக்களத்து ஏதிலர் போல வரும்; ஈரும் இருள்மாலை). The teaches says the Kural only implies that the hostility lies in absence, but the couplet states it outright (காதலர் இல்வழி). The venba's real addition, sweet to the companioned (செல்சார் வுடையார்க்கு இனியவாய்), is small.

Both see the konrai as gold (பொன்செய் புனையிழை; சுடுபொன் அன்ன கொன்றை), and Kuruntokai 21 refuses the season's witness (யானோ தேறேன்). Ainkurunuru 432's praise of his road (நன்றே காதலர் சென்ற ஆறே) is uncertain in tone. Konrai as season sign is stock, so this is at most a shared image.
links.text_issue: Line 5 of Kuruntokai 21 is a repaired reading; Ainkurunuru 432 is marked uncertain.

links.reason: Natrinai 134 has the mother send the girl to the millet (ஏயள்மன் யாயும்), and 122 says the millet will be guarded (கடியும் உண்டு என) and the mother frowns (அமரா முகத்தினள்). 122 does not foresee the end of the guarding; it names the guarding to come, so the 'cover and clock' scheme is imposed. Millet guarding as cover is a stock kurinji setting.
links.text_issue: Natrinai 134 line 6 differs strongly from sangamtamil.com; the poem is marked uncertain.

links.reason: Sea and raft are shared (காமக் கடல் ... ஏமப் புணை இல்; கரை காணாப் பௌவத்துக் ... திரை தரப் புணை பெற்று). The Kural speaks during absence and the kali at the lovers' return (விரைவனர் காதலர் புகுதர), so the two are not incompatible. The teaches itself reconciles them, which is qualification, not tension.

Muthumozhikkanchi 69 adds a condition on the judge (பொருள்நசை வேட்கையோன் முறைசெயல் பொய்) to Kural 541's procedure (ஓர்ந்துகண் ணோடாது இறைபுரிந்து). But கண்ணோடாது already excludes partiality, of which greed is a kind, so the addition is thinner than 'says nothing of the judge's appetites' suggests.

Kural 370 promises an unshifting nature once craving goes (அவாநீப்பின் ... பேரா இயற்கை தரும்); Kural 380 says nothing is stronger than fate (ஊழிற் பெருவலி யாவுள). The note does not say on which reading release and fate conflict, and the teaches only describes their order in the book.

Kuruntokai 319 sets the evening rain (மாலைவந் தன்று மாரி) as the hour when the stag clasps its doe (மடப்பிணை தழீஇ) and the elephant joins its mate (பிடியொடு பொருந்தி), and then fears for her life (என்னாந் ... இன்னுயிர் நிலையே). That gives a cause for Kural 1221's bare claim that the hour eats the lives of the wedded (மணந்தார் உயிருண்ணும் வேலை).

பெருஞ்சோறு is really shared (பெருஞ்சோற்று மிகுபதம் வரையாது கொடுத்தோய், Purananuru 2; பெருஞ்சோறு உகுத்தற்கு எறியும் ... முரசே, Patitruppattu 30). But the teaches conflates the great rice with the blood-soaked offering to the god (அரும்பெறல் பிண்டம் ... இரும்பலி), and 'binds the warriors' is not in the text. The father-son tie and the rite's name rest on the colophons (பெருஞ்சோற்றுநிலை, patron lines).

The contrast is real: Kural 1259's heart defects to union (நெஞ்சம் கலத்தல் உறுவது கண்டு), while Kalittokai 87 gives up sulking at a shameless man (நாண் இலன் ஆயின் ... ஊடுதல் என்னோ, இனி) and asks the heart to watch. But the deciding lines 11, 12, 15 and 16 are absent from another edition, so the link rests on doubtful text.
links.text_issue: Lines 11, 12, 15 and 16 are not in sangamtamil.com.

links.reason: The verbal tie is மடி: மடியிலா மன்னவன் (Kural 610) and பனிஎன மடியாய், with மாரி என்னாய் (fragment 4). The fragment applies tirelessness to campaigning through rain and cold, with an army camped in a foreign land (வேறுபுலத்து இறுத்த). That is a specific application of the Kural's general virtue.

Both have the bangles report his leaving (துறைவன் துறந்தமை தூற்றா ... வளை; துறைகெழு கொண்கன் பிரிந்தென ... எல்வளை நீங்கிய நிலையே). The contrast between bangles that gossip and a bard who must carry the sight is real, but 'the couplet compresses a scene' claims a descent. Slipping bangles are a stock sign.
links.text_issue: Line 1 of Ainkurunuru 140 is a repaired reading.

links.reason: Purananuru 66 ranks the defeated king, ashamed of his back wound (புறப்புண் நாணி, வடக் கிருந்தோனே), above Karikal (நின்னினும் நல்லன்). The Pattinappalai's catalogue gives the ethic of not turning back only to his side (ஒருவேமெனப் புறக்கொடாது). Same patron, same ethic, opposite placement: the pair shows what the praise leaves out.
links.text_issue: Line 290 is a repaired reading (ஒருவேனெப் to ஒருவேமெனப்), and whose men lines 289 to 291 describe is not certain.

links.reason: Natrinai 251 begs the millet to ripen late (நீடினை விளைமோ வாழிய தினையே), and 259 finds the ears dry-ripe (புலர் பதம் கொண்டன ஏனற் குரலே), so the bond becomes hard to keep (அரிய போலக் காண்பேன்). The colophons call for marriage (வரைவு கடாயது) and announce confinement. Before and after of the same clock, in the Tamil.

Thirikadugam 9 lists desire for women not one's own among what fools love (உரிமையில் பெண்டிரைக் காமுற்று வாழ்தல் ... முழுமக்கள் காதலவை); 19 puts the man at another's door by night among those who hang by a thread (பிறன்கடை நின்றொழுகுவான் ... தூங்குபவர்). The teaches is true but thin: it says only that the book condemns adultery twice, from two angles.

poems.note: The wet pot in heavy rain is joined to his heart by ஏற்றாங்கு, so it is an open comparison.
The bear tearing open the anthill for food could stand for his going for wealth and ruining her beauty, but only the mood of harm is clear.
The heron that goes to see another bird's chick and stays all day invites a reading of the man with another woman, but neither the poem nor the blank thurai states that situation.
The ripe jackfruit given as a feast to the monkey can be paired with ripening love (காமம் கனிவது) and welcoming him, but the stated situation is fear of the night path.
The poem states the parallel itself: the mullai longs for the rains, and her beauty longs for his chariot.

iraicchi.act: the tiger unites with its female and its distress ends (பெண்பாற் புணர்ந்து ... பையுள் தீரும்)
iraicchi.sense: the sickness the hill man caused is cured by union with him, not by the velan's rite

poems.note: Lines 2 to 4 (கறிய, கழங்கு மெய்ப்படூஉ, புனவர் புணர்த்த மெய்ம்மை அன்ன) look corrupt, so the carrier's act is read with caution.

The tiger that kills the tusker and leaves the she-elephant mourning (பிடி புலம்ப) maps to the gossip that breaks the union and leaves her alone; the tiger could also be read as the man who ruined her.
Lines 1 and 2 are lost and line 4 is broken, so nothing can be tagged.
The kanchi whose soft branch the farmers bend and which still sheds its pollen on them maps to the wife who is bent by his wrong and still hides it and receives him.

iraicchi.act: united with its mate, the red dog passes by and does not seize the doe with her fawn
iraicchi.sense: the road itself showed him care for a mate, and he hurried home to her

poems.note: The punnai pollen that settles on the heron's white back each time the wind blows maps to the name 'his woman' that has settled on her and cannot be removed; the second pair is a reading, not certain.
